item.title: Smoked Signals: The Tipline for 2 February 2026
item.description: The US antitrust agencies are targeting ephemeral messaging once again. This time, the Federal Trade Commission has accused Amazon executives of deleting Signal messages for three and a half years after the antitrust investigation into its business began. Amazon lawyers and executives also altered internal memos to remove language about anticompetitive conduct, the FTC claimed. Also in Tipline, An...

item.title: HPE lobbyists ordered to turn over comms
item.description: Lobbyists hired to secure approval for Hewlett Packard Enterprise/Juniper Networks must share communications they had with the Department of Justice related to the deal’s controversial approval, a California federal court has ruled.

item.title: Headwinds: The Briefing for 3 February 2026
item.description: The EU has escalated another probe into a Chinese company under the Foreign Subsidies Regulation, targeting wind turbine maker Goldwind. It comes soon after the agency also launched an in-depth investigation into security company Nuctech, prompting a Chinese business lobby group to reiterate concerns that the rulebook is disproportionately scrutinising China-backed investment in the bloc. Also in ...

item.title: US think tank targets serial acquisition theory in Canadian consultation
item.description: Updated draft unilateral conduct guidance from Canada’s Competition Bureau incorrectly targets serial acquisitions, miscontrues the purpose of structural remedies and could "inadvertently" discourage beneficial self-preferencing, two policy groups with links to digital platforms have said.

item.title: Netherlands launches first no-poach probe
item.description: The Netherlands Authority for Consumers and Markets has raided an IT company as part of its first-ever probe into a possible no-poach conspiracy, with the agency noting that further inspections could follow.

item.title: Repsol to challenge €20.5 million margin squeeze fine in Spain
item.description: One of Spain's leading fuel suppliers will appeal against a €20.5 million fine by the country’s antitrust watchdog for squeezing the margins of low-cost service stations when Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.

item.title: CMA criticises tribunal’s by object assessment in standalone RPM ruling
item.description: The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority has told an appellate court that the country’s specialist antitrust tribunal “fell into error” when ruling that a major footwear supplier’s online sales policy amounted to a by object infringement.

item.title: X-factor: The Tipline for 3 February 2026
item.description: Elon Musk has further consolidated his business empire by having SpaceX acquire xAI. The formation of the $1.2 trillion company on Monday follows xAI’s acquisition of the social network X last year. Musk said the company would be “one of the most ambitious, vertically integrated innovation engines on (and off) Earth”. item.title: GOP challenge Netflix on YouTube rivalry claim
item.description: Republicans on the Senate Antitrust Subcommittee have rejected claims from the Netflix chief executive that YouTube is a primary competitor.

item.title: Kirkland, Covington steer closing of complex Disney/NFL deal
item.description: The Department of Justice has permitted Disney to acquire NFL Media in exchange for a 10% equity stake in ESPN.
